study type: post-hoc analysis of secondary outcome parameters of a prospective observational study
exposure: acid-base and metabolic parameters from arterial umbilical cord blood (pH-value, bicarbonate, base-excess, and lactate)
cohort: The study included 77 neonates: 14 preterm neonates with respiratory support (mean gestational age 31.4 +/- 4.1 weeks; mean birth weight 1,690 +/- 640 g) and 63 term neonates without respiratory support (gestational age 38.7 +/- 0.8 weeks; birth weight 3,258 +/- 443 g).
finding: In preterm neonates with respiratory support, higher lactate levels were significantly associated with lower crSO2 and SpO2, while no significant associations were observed in term neonates without respiratory support.
gest_age: preterm (mean gestational age 31.4 +/- 4.1 weeks) and term (38.7 +/- 0.8 weeks)
birth_weight: preterm (mean birth weight 1,690 +/- 640 g) and term (3,258 +/- 443 g)
